findings: TASK 1: EDITOR IDENTITY LINKS IN OR BESIDE THE SCOPE. Within the 267 TEI-rule volumes, the only editor identity links are the three split-set second parts. They carry 10,616 persName corresp attributes, 9,215 inside documents: 2,003 from/to and 7,212 untyped. They point at 634 distinct entries in the sibling lists, but only 122 of those have an authority crosswalk id and only 52 a POCOM slug. As silver identity rows this is 985 slug-bearing from/to heads, all 1900-1945, all post-naming heads, 26 people. The live v50 index holds these links as 5,530 orphan person_mentions rows over 2,089 documents, with 0 persons rows, and no other scope volume has a single person_mentions row. No other persName in the 267 carries corresp or ref: type and corresp are the only persName attributes present. In the 285 list volumes there is 1 cross-volume link, outside any document, and 2 dangling ones; the corresp attributes in frus1914-16 are not person links. frus1941-43 has 81 persons rows in the index but no body link. Beside the scope, the 1873 pair has 57-entry lists with 934 linked from/to mentions over 41 distinct entries, but the crosswalk holds exactly one entry per volume (Hamilton Fish). The only pre-1900 editor-asserted identity that reaches POCOM without name matching is therefore one person, on 470 rows. frus1873p1v2's 454 rows are orphans in the live index until the #1291 v51 reindex.

TASK 2: THE SILVER SET EXISTS AND IS LARGE, BUT ONLY AFTER 1900. From/to heads with an editor link whose crosswalk carries a POCOM slug, by band (MEASURED, silver2.py): 1861-1899 459 (Fish only); 1900-1929 7,097 (14 volumes, 62 people); 1930-1945 1,526 (12 volumes, 90 people); 1946- 23,655 (181 volumes, 587 people). On the positive rows, POCOM surname x year agrees 0.9993 / 0.9982 / 0.9624 when it picks one person. A negative silver set also exists: people the editors identified whom the registry does not join to POCOM, 1,713 / 1,749 / 16,066 heads. Including its false picks, the same rule's precision falls to 0.972 / 0.939 / 0.863 (INFERRED, combined_precision.py). A positive-only silver set therefore flatters any surname rule by roughly 3 to 10 points per band. The error classes it exposes are namesakes (the Rostows, 243 rows; Taylor, 115), relatives (Kathleen Harriman), and senators or consuls sharing a chief's surname (Morgan, Fletcher). The Source Explorer post + surname rule (COMB) is barely scorable on silver. Per band, route A only, it made 31/31, 68/68 and 158/158 picks, plus 408/408 pre-1900 picks that are all Fish. The pooled post-1905 98.6% corroboration figure is 475/482 'one'-class heads, mostly 1930-1945 and 1946-; it rests on 23 both-same picks in 1900-1929 (relabel_bands.py). Source Explorer's pre-1906 gate means shipped COMB never runs on silver except for the 1873 pair.

TASK 3: WHAT SILVER CAN LICENSE. (a) A development and regression corpus for identity rules: golden cases, threshold tuning, and namesake and relative guards, including 2,133 'several'-class heads in 1900-1929 where the head names the post. (b) A measured error profile of POCOM surname x year on post-naming heads, including the negative set. (c) After a small transfer check, an agreement estimate for untagged post-1900 volumes, whose head format is close to silver's: 75.8 / 95.2 / 89.6% post-naming untagged vs 99.4 / 95.7 / 86.4% silver. (d) Identity for the split parts: 985 heads, and 2,261 slug-bearing links of any type, can be shown today without any rule, once the cross-part join is fixed. That is §4.0's step 0.

TASK 3: WHAT SILVER CANNOT LICENSE, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE UNTAGGED PRE-1900 POPULATION. (1) Header format: 95.7% of untagged 1861-1899 from/to heads are bare honorifics ('Mr. Seward to Mr. Adams') and 1.3% name a post; outside Fish, silver is 0% bare honorific. The evidence route differs too: post-1900 silver names the post in the head, while pre-1900 identity must come from the Source Explorer chapter. (2) POCOM coverage: silver positives are POCOM people by construction. Unknown-class rows are 2.5% of 1900-1929 silver heads vs 13.0% of untagged 1861-1899 heads, where most are foreign envoys, legation secretaries, chargés and consuls. The 1861-1899 negative set is empty. (3) Circularity: silver slugs come from name-matching joins. frus-name-authority matches on exact, alternate and fuzzy names; the OH registry's merge method is undocumented. A silver slug therefore almost never contradicts the printed surname, so surname-mismatch errors cannot appear and only same-surname errors are tested. Office years come from the same POCOM dates the rule uses. label-validation's pre-1900 route B is POCOM-derived, and route A there is Fish alone. (4) Concentration: the effective n is people and volumes, not rows. Walter Hines Page is 23.6% of 1900-1929 silver heads, and 1861-1899 is one person. (5) Silver has no Seward class: 8,306 untagged 1861-1899 heads are resolved only by the Secretary-over-assistant convention, and no list volume covers 1861-69. It also has no acting-officer or chargé-signing class, and no foreign-legation-chapter class in bare-honorific form.

TASK 3: MINIMAL KEYED SAMPLE (INFERRED from sample-design.json and chapter-context S1). Silver can replace most post-1900 keying but none of the pre-1900 keying. Three sizes, by the claim to be made:
(A) One pooled 'Possible identity (from filing context)' tier for 1861-1899 heads where surname x year and the chapter post agree: 100 blind decided rows from that two-signal stratum, 25 each from 1861-69, the 1870s, the 1880s and the 1890s. Zero errors gives a lower bound of 0.963, one error 0.9455. That detects a fall from silver's ~0.99 to 0.93 (n=60) but only marginally to 0.95 (n=110).
(B) Per-class claims: add 60 several-narrowed-by-chief/Department rows, 60 Seward-convention rows from 1861-69, 60 nobody/contradicted rows, 50 foreign-legation or notes-chapter rows and 50 enclosure heads, about 380 decided rows in all.
(C) The full chapter-context design of 450-500 rows, which adds about 100 rows of surname-only picks where the chapter abstains, to price coverage beyond the two-signal set.
The M1a 300-row instrument stays unstratified. Its 100 pre-1910 rows (75 pre-1900 plus 25 from 1904) price the surname rule only and hold 12 several-class rows, so a zero-error lower bound there is just 0.7575. Key them blind and post-stratify them, but they do not substitute for (A). After 1900, silver cuts the instrument's 200 rows from 1910 on to a transfer check: about 50-60 blind rows from untagged post-1910 volumes, weighted to unknown- and nobody-class picks, which silver positives exclude and the negatives cover only where the registry holds the person.

TASK 4: CLAUDE PRE-FILLING CONTAMINATES THE INSTRUMENT IN FOUR WAYS. (1) Anchoring: a confirm-or-reject pass measures acceptance of a candidate, not identity. The only precedent cannot size the effect: M2a seeded 88 editor spans, 0 were removed outright and all 35 'rejections' were boundary edits (MEASURED). No wrong seed was planted, and the marked arm's 88/88 overlap appears to be scored against its own seeds (INFERRED). (2) Self-scoring: a Claude or rule arm scored on rows it pre-filled measures agreement with itself. (3) Model memory: a Claude pre-fill can import an identity no local source supports, and 18.6% of marked correspondent mentions have none (DOCUMENTED, prior answer), so the gold becomes partly model-authored. (4) Rule leakage: showing the surname x year or chapter pick pre-scores those arms.

TASK 4: A DESIGN THAT AVOIDS CONTAMINATION.
(i) Freeze every rule and prompt, with a committed hash, before drawing the sample. Tune only on silver and never on the keyed rows or the 64 published M2a documents.
(ii) Blind phase: the keying sheet shows the head, dateline, chapter path and document text, plus a neutral POCOM search, with no ranked candidates, no in-office flag and no machine pick. The owner records a slug, 'not in POCOM' or 'cannot tell', with a one-line evidence note. The file is locked with a sha256, the stage_m2a staged_sha256 pattern.
(iii) Reveal phase: after the lock, show the surname x year, COMB and Claude candidates. The owner records a separate post-reveal verdict and reason. Every arm is scored against the blind column only, and the reveal switch rate is reported as its own measurement.
(iv) If speed requires pre-filling: randomise rows within strata into blind and pre-filled halves, and plant plausible wrong candidates (same surname, another post or a concurrent namesake) in about 10-15% of pre-filled rows. The acceptance rate of planted errors estimates anchoring; with 0 of 30 accepted the upper bound is 11.35%, with 0 of 50 it is 7.14%. The difference in agreement between the halves is the anchoring effect.
(v) Claude adjudication and synthesis run only after the lock. Claude may draft the evidence sentence shown in the app, never the verdict shown during keying.
caveats: Silver is agreement with an editor link joined through the person-authority crosswalk and the OH registry or name-authority overlay to a POCOM slug. Parts of that chain are name matching, so it is not ground truth. Mention-grain Wilson intervals overstate certainty; volume bootstraps are given, and the effective sample is closer to the distinct people (1 / 62 / 90 / 587).
The negative silver set assumes that a crosswalked person with no slug is not a POCOM officeholder. Possible registry misses were flagged by forename initial (2 / 8 / 40) but not verified by reading.

The head-format classifier is regex and was not validated by reading. Its post word list includes Department and General. It was applied identically to silver and to untagged heads, so the comparison is like-for-like, but its absolute shares are approximate. silver.py's own head-format table missed honorifics inside the span and is superseded by silver2.py.
The S rule is measure_pocom.py imported verbatim: min-to-max year spans, a +-1 document year, surname_of dropping tokens under 3 letters and splitting multi-token surnames (De Long reads as Long).

Populations: silver draws on the 285 list volumes plus the 3 split parts, which matches neither the app view (267 volumes / 198,936 documents) nor the TEI-rule scope (267 / 197,534). Untagged comparison figures are TEI-rule-scope from/to heads read from the TEI (60,645 in 1861-1899). The strata counts are chapter-context's 61-volume head grain, a different denominator. Figures from different populations are never combined here.

Bands use the TEI frus:doc-dateTime-min year. label-validation's per-band table covers only the 33 post-1905 list volumes whose coverage starts by 1950, plus its 15-volume proxy, as that census exported them.

The live index is at v50 and predates #1291 and #1292. Split-part and frus1873p1v2 rows will change after a reindex, and the Source Explorer tallies used for strata predate #1292 in part: coverage arm B applied title repairs.
That the M2a marked arm was scored against its own seeds is inferred from equal counts (88), not from matching spans one by one.
notMeasured: Any identity precision on the untagged pre-1900 population: 0 of 300 instrument rows are keyed, and no other keyed identity exists.
The Source Explorer chapter-post rule on silver beyond label-validation's existing rows. The Swift harness was not re-run, and the post-#1292 classifier was not applied to silver.
A head-post plus surname rule (the post-1900 analogue of COMB) on silver's 2,133 several-class heads in 1900-1929.
Claude adjudication or synthesis of any kind: no LLM API was called and no corpus text left the machine.
The size of the anchoring effect: no planted-error or split-half keying data exists anywhere in the record.
How the OH people registry merged FRUS list entries with POCOM records: undocumented in the repository examined.
What list form the index read to produce frus1941-43's 81 persons rows, and whether those rows are identity-bearing.

findings: I measured every job population from the stores with scripts in YOUR_DIR, and they pass their positive controls. pools.py reproduces the store row totals (245,747 / 1,261,852 / 2,597,043), the 197,534 documents and 679,401,514 characters, and the gold counts of §2.2/§2.3 exactly, with 0 span/text mismatches. se_pocom_cases.py reproduces summary.json in all four arm×band cells.

The agreement arm now has a corpus-scale census, which the feasibility assessment §4.b2 said did not exist: 1,310,341 spans, 758,194 (document, surface-key) pairs, in 190,658 of 197,534 TEI-rule documents (96.5%, INFERRED share). The key is grains.py's surface_key, so the pair count is not the census-K2 grain of §2.1.

Job A has two defensible readings of 'three-way union minus the agreement arm'. The literal exact-span difference is 1,886,490 spans. The real adjudication queue, which drops spans already overlapping an agreement span, is 1,526,825 spans / 1,051,899 pairs / 179,212 documents. That is larger than the agreement arm itself and weighted to 1930-1945 (517,620 spans). Control-only is small (214,933 spans); sweep-only is most of the queue (1,485,681).

At the recorded prices, A and B are the only Claude jobs costing hundreds of dollars (INFERRED). Sonnet 5 in batch with caching at low effort: A queue $146 / $223 / $1,130, B $129 / $209 / $1,113. Opus 5 is roughly 2.0-2.6× that. Standard, uncached, high effort is roughly 3.5-4× the batch figure. The high end of every range is driven by a one-request-per-document design with unmerged windows and a 6,000-token prefix, not by the pools.

Jobs C and D are cheap (INFERRED). Source Explorer × POCOM adjudication of 13,907 rows is $4-$13 on Sonnet 5 in batch ($9-$33 on Opus 5), and $17-$92 with document text. Guides for 267 volumes cost $5.5-$8.1 on Sonnet 5 in batch ($54-$92 on Opus 5 standard high). Per-chapter guides (9,954 chapters at 1,500 words) are the only synthesis variant in the hundreds: $174-$249 Sonnet 5 batch, $1,897-$3,153 Opus 5 standard high.

The whole headline set A + B + C + D prices at $284 / $444 / $2,265 on Sonnet 5 (batch, cache, low effort) and $568 / $1,048 / $5,833 on Opus 5. Standard high effort is $835 / $1,582 / $8,805 and $1,757 / $3,829 / $22,548 (INFERRED).

Pilots are not cost-constrained (INFERRED). All four Opus 5 pilots at 3 replicates, standard, high effort total about $25 central and $51 high. Of that, D on the 24 M2a volumes is $19. A and B on the 64 documents are $1.4-$1.6 central each.

Job A's value is bounded before any model runs (INFERRED from §2.2 plus the measured gold pools). On the 64 documents at most 62 of 330 queue pairs can be true (≤18.8%), so a verifier spends about 5 verdicts per recoverable name. Its output-token cost is slightly overstated because cost_model's shape-B accept rate of 0.49 is above that ceiling.

Local alternative (INFERRED from the sweep's throughput): A+B+C+D on Qwen3-14B no-think takes about 361-376 Studio hours (15.0-15.7 days, longer than the 11.55-day sweep) and 32-45 kWh (about $5-$11). A 27-31B judge would take about 2×. Scenario ranges are wide: 96-1,522 h for A alone, depending on packing and prefix re-prefill. Local verification quality is unmeasured.

Pricing provenance: cost_model.py records no pricing date and no source. It carries only a 'DOCUMENTED $/MTok' comment and tokenizer-multiplier comments. Its prices, batch and cache multipliers, and cache minimums are identical to the bundled claude-api skill reference table cached 2026-06-24. The feasibility assessment's own dollar lines cite a different source, RIDE §4.4's 2026-08 pricing.

Compared with the in-session prior answer ($460-$700 Sonnet 5 to judge candidates with whole documents): verifying only the net queue with ±300-character windows is $146-$1,130, central $223 (INFERRED). But the populations differ, since the prior figure covered all candidates, so this is not like-for-like.
caveats: Every token count is converted from characters: cost_model.py's measured Qwen3 chars/token (4.6442) divided by its inferred per-model multipliers (Opus 5 1.00-1.69). No tokenizer endpoint was called, so token and dollar figures can be off by up to about ±40%.
Thinking tokens, cache hit rates inside batches, output tokens per verdict (5-20) and rows per request (50/25/10) are cost_model.py's inferred assumptions, applied unchanged. They are not measured.

Job C counts are the pre-#1292 approximation from summary.json. By the time I finished, measure-se-pocom held classifier outputs (classified/*.jsonl) but no count file. My post-#1292 counts are a sensitivity check: they run measure_chapter_rule.py's analysis-side title repair (arm B) on top of the already-fixed classifier, so they may double-count repairs.

The job C payload design is mine: candidates are same-surname POCOM officeholders live in the document year ±1, plus the holders on that date of the posts the chapter hypothesis names. Career lines are restricted to the volume window ±1. A different prompt design changes the per-case size (mean 557-952 chars).

Job D's 1,500-word output uses 6.011 chars/word measured on FRUS R-0 prose, not on generated text. Chapters are live-index volume_structures sections that list documents directly, not only divType=chapter. Header samples come from the owner's live index at v50 (document_cache rows), which is an index population, not the TEI-rule document count.

Local hours rest on assumptions. The 12.1× decode/prefill cost ratio comes from the Air pilot (§4.8) and is applied to the Studio sweep's 4-worker wall-clock aggregate. The low scenario assumes KV reuse of the instruction prefix. The 1.9-2.2× factor for a 27-31B judge is a parameter-ratio judgement. 90-120 W and $0.15-0.25/kWh are side.json assumptions.

Pilot costs assume 3 replicates. The 64 gold documents have published error lists (leakage), and the prior answer's minimum detectable effect there is about 0.05 F1. A cheap pilot can screen a model; it cannot establish corpus precision.
The job A yield ceiling (≤62 true of 330 queue pairs) is for n = 64 documents and uses the presence grain. It is a ceiling, not a precision, and per-band precision varies roughly ±0.13.

Pool counts are in the TEI-rule population (267 volumes / 197,534 documents). They must not be combined with app-view figures (267/268 volumes, about 199k documents). The live-index header row count (198,821) was used only for sampling.
Nothing was sent off the machine and no LLM or count_tokens endpoint was called. Scripts suppressed Python bytecode writes. Everything was written only under YOUR_DIR.

methodProblems: FOOTNOTE UNDERCOUNT (numerator and denominator from different populations). The footnote-span figure takes its numerator only from the 354 documents whose whole-document alignment succeeded: 273 + 16 sweep, 118 + 13 control. Its denominator is every span in all 400 documents. The 985 sweep and 512 control spans in the 46 unaligned documents were labelled 'no_alignment' in flat-spans.jsonl and never tested for footnote membership. A TEI-derived character map (v2_flat.py), which reconstructs R-0 exactly in 400/400 documents, gives 355/5,188 = 6.8% (sweep) and 182/2,694 = 6.8% (control), against the reported 5.6% / 4.9%. The unaligned documents are skewed to later bands (2/11/15/18), so the per-band figures are biased where footnotes are densest: 1946- sweep is 13.6%, not 11.0%.

END-TO-END BREAKDOWN MISCLASSIFIED. The 812 sweep and 401 control placements reported as 'unverified' are all correct against full ground truth: 4,581 = 3,769 + 812 and 2,393 = 1,992 + 401, with 0 wrong. The residual is 4.9% / 4.3% of all spans refused and 6.8% in or straddling footnotes, not '3-6% refused, ~5% footnote'.

WRONG METRIC FOR THE CONVERTER ROUTE. 'Only 43.8% / 35.1% of surfaces are unique in their document' is used to say a text-splitting converter route 'has the same ambiguity problem'. A route that wraps every occurrence of a detected surface does not need uniqueness. Its cost is the occurrences it wraps that no detector tagged. I reproduced the identity-silver measurement with my own scripts (in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jbotts-Development-FRUS-Explorer--claude-worktrees-234-feasibility-assessment-518fe5/1ccebcd5-11bc-42dd-8b13-b2025658e2f3/scratchpad/reframe/verify-measure-silver): an ElementTree TEI scan, an ElementTree POCOM loader, SQL joins on the live index (mode=ro), and span-level reads of the M2a stores. Almost every count reproduces exactly, and the headline conclusions stand. The main defects are one double-counted figure, a band that is mislabelled and pooled, and two undisclosed limits on the precision and circularity figures.

CONFIRMED (MEASURED):
- **Links inside the scope.** Only the 3 split-set parts carry editor identity links: 10,616 corresp, 9,215 inside documents, 1,962 from/to in heads. They reach 634 targets, 122 with a crosswalk id and 52 with a POCOM slug, and give 985 slug-bearing heads.
- **Live index v50.** The split parts have 0 persons rows and 5,530 orphan mentions. frus1873p1v2 has 454 orphans. frus1941-43 has 81 persons rows and no mentions.
- **Pre-1900 links.** The 1873 pair's only crosswalked entry is Hamilton Fish, so pre-1900 silver is one person on 459 heads.
- **Silver sizes** by band: 459 / 7,097 / 1,526 / 23,655 heads, over 1 / 62 / 90 / 587 persons.
- **POCOM surname x year agreement** on positive silver: 459/459, 4,075/4,078, 1,136/1,138 and 15,306/15,904. This is agreement given a unique pick, not a precision on the untagged population.
- **Negative silver:** 1,713 / 1,749 / 16,066 heads with 115 / 72 / 1,840 false picks, and the arithmetic giving 0.972 / 0.939 / 0.863 over positive plus negative.
- **Other figures:** join provenance (1946- entirely registry-route); the 475/482 corroboration figure; all sample-size arithmetic; the M1a instrument (300 rows, 0 keyed; pre-1910 S classes 63 / 12 / 8 / 17).
- **M2a.** The marked layer equals the seeded spans in 64 of 64 documents, so the 'scored against its own seeds' claim moves from INFERRED to MEASURED.
- **Head format.** Untagged 1861-1899 heads (n = 60,645, TEI-rule scope, document-year band) are about 96% honorific-led, with office words in at most 1.3%.

ERRORS AND UNDISCLOSED LIMITS:
1. **Double count.** silver.py counts each head twice in its concentration tables. Walter Hines Page has 1,678 heads, not 3,356; the 23.6% share is right.
2. **The '1900-1929' silver band is 1910-1919 only.** For 1900-1909 (12,405 untagged heads, 20 volumes, 68% honorific-led) there is no silver, no Source Explorer chapter post after 1905, and no stratum in the proposed keyed sample. 'Close to silver' and 'silver can replace most post-1900 keying' do not hold for that decade; they do hold from 1910 on.
3. **Band key differs from the assessment.** The measurement bands by document year; the assessment's band_of reads the year in the volume id. Using the assessment's key moves 101 heads and changes the 1930-1945 figure from 0.939 to 0.930.
4. **The combined 'precision' excludes unscoreable picks.** S picks on linked heads with no crosswalk id (274 / 539 / 1,490) are outside it. In 1930-1945 they outnumber the scored picks, so the figure is conditional on registry coverage.
5. **Negative-silver errors are concentrated.** They come mostly from a few namesake pairs: Lyndon B. Johnson read as U. Alexis Johnson (649), McGeorge Bundy as William P. Bundy (619), and Woodrow Wilson as Charles S. Wilson (88). Only about 18 rows look like registry misses. The negatives are genuine, but the effective sample is a handful of people.
6. **Circularity is overstated.** Name matching is documented only for the overlay route. All 23,655 1946- silver heads come through the registry route, whose merge method is undocumented.
7. **Smaller label issues.**
   - There are 286 list volumes in the TEI, not 285; frus1981-88v16 is missing from the crosswalk.
   - 79% of the 1930-1945 both-same rows rest on POCOM-derived gold.
   - The planted-error bounds are Wilson bounds and are not named as such.
   - The strata sizes predate #1292: 8.9% of 1861-1899 documents changed their suggestions after it, mostly additions.

NOT RE-DERIVED: the chapter-rule strata and the post-1905 COMB rule, because they need the Swift harness. No identity precision exists for the untagged pre-1900 population, since 0 of the 300 M1a rows are keyed. Populations: silver uses the 286 list volumes plus the 3 split parts; the untagged comparisons use TEI-rule-scope heads banded by document year. Neither is the app view.

Population: 411 marked rows with surname Hunter dated 1865-01-01..1866-07-26, POCOM's gap between his chief-clerk end (1855-05-07) and second-assistant start (1866-07-27). Rows are head-from 197, head-to 204, enclosure 10; kinds are country 270, foreign legation 133, topical 8. Source Explorer: 269 already shown, 108 newly shown by #1292, 34 still none. POCOM chapter rule: 0 corroborated in every arm. S_before 269 contradicted / 142 no hypothesis; S_after 377 contradicted (375 'holder in no post on date', 2 'within 180 days') / 34 none; T_after 408 / 3. The sender rule decided 0 of 411, since 194 of 197 head-from documents already carry 'Department of State' in the dateline. The non-identity label reads 'the Department of State' for 193 of 197 head-from rows (1 'U.S. mission in Spain', 3 none) and 173 of 204 head-to rows (S_after); T_after 194 and 200. The filing role is right where the identity rule fails.
caveats: Every corroboration and contradiction count measures agreement between two rules, not correctness. The chapter rule naming one person is a ceiling on what it could get right, never a precision.

Two populations are kept apart. ROW figures use the TEI-rule marked layer restricted to the 70 no-list volumes up to 1905. The 1861-1899 band is by volume year: 61 volumes, 84,234 rows, 30,864 documents holding rows. DOCUMENT-reach figures use the live-index export for the same volumes: 32,809 documents 1861-1899 and 6,222 in 1900-1905. PR #1292's 76.9%/85.9% used the app year over all 81 export volumes (32,478 documents) and is not directly comparable.

Every label precision estimate comes from a population other than the target (1861-1899 no-list rows). The 1873 volumes carry lists and are 1872-73 only. Their evidence covers 31 distinct list entries, 409 of 651 judged rows have Department-only evidence, and there are no legation chapters. Headers that print an office are 2.1% of 1861-1899 documents and 20.7% of 1900-1905 documents, and are selected toward unusual documents. The post-1905 volumes run the classifier outside its design era.

The U.S.-mission chapter kind, the label map, the evidence parsers for role text and header offices, the city/country crosswalk and the addressee heuristic are this program's own judgement. Two revisions of the parser and judge followed reading wrong examples from the first proxy run: a place-less role such as the Department matches without a place; an office 'at Rome' in 1873 reads as Italy; Cairo and Alexandria compare as one Egyptian post; memorandum headers are skipped; 'President X' counts as U.S. only for U.S. presidents; and diplomatic labels require a country title. The proxies could therefore be flattered by tuning.

The 1861-1899 row-grain header proxy is small (106 strict independent sides in S_after). The weak 1905 'Minister X' evidence (720 sides) cannot separate a U.S. minister from a foreign 'Minister Wu'. None of those 720 was judged wrong-kind, but that class cannot catch the error.

Classifier inputs come from the live index at version 50, before #1291. #1291 changed person-list joins, not headers, datelines or section structure (INFERRED), so these classifications should not move at v51, but that was not re-run.
The harness does not run Source Explorer's enclosure pass, and the label is refused for enclosure rows by design. 23,128 of 84,234 rows (1861-1899) are enclosure rows.

The Hunter population window (1865-01-01..1866-07-26, any side) is this program's definition, from POCOM's dates. The Seward classes reproduce seward_crosstab.py's population and signature rule exactly.
The addressee heuristic in at_risk.py counts OCR-damaged Secretary names ('Mr. Hazy', 'Air. Seward') as non-Department. Its 'not a Secretary' counts are therefore upper bounds.
notMeasured: True precision of the filing-role label on 1861-1899 no-list rows. No keyed sample exists; only the proxies above do.
Label precision inside pre-1900 foreign-legation chapters. The 1873 volumes have none and 1861-1899 heads rarely print offices, so no independent evidence was available.
U.S. mission country precision in 1900-1905: those headers do not print the post, so the 720 'Minister X' sides are kind-only.
The row-level label error rate in the 305 legation documents filed under a different parent country (S_after). The count is measured; the effect on each row is not.
Correctness of any POCOM identity pick, and how many of the 2,062 (S_after) or 2,536 (T_after) contradictions are POCOM gaps, such as Hunter, versus surname-rule errors.

A full census of chapter-title forms the merged normaliser still misses. Only those the earlier Python approximation happened to read were counted: 148 documents 1861-1899 plus 9 in 1900-1905, e.g. glued 'CorrespondenceArgentine Republic'.
Label reach or precision at index version 51, and label behaviour for enclosures through the app's enclosure pass.
The app-side cost or UI wording of a filing-role label, and whether Source Explorer's shown cards and a People-side label would ever disagree.

v2:9fcab44a471cc821b776ea189271c1855f3c2.summary:
I re-derived 12 of the measure-se-pocom figures with six scripts of my own, and every one I tested reproduced exactly or within small differences I can explain. Only the chief-of-mission half of the headline corroboration table went untested. The scripts read the TEI, the marked store, POCOM (via ElementTree) and the classifier output directly, not the measurement's code. Scripts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jbotts-Development-FRUS-Explorer--claude-worktrees-234-feasibility-assessment-518fe5/1ccebcd5-11bc-42dd-8b13-b2025658e2f3/scratchpad/reframe/verify-measure-se-pocom/ (v_population.py, v_shown_labels.py, v_proxy1873.py, v_dept_corroboration.py, v_header_proxy.py, v_atrisk_sender.py); outputs are in its out/ subfolder.

What reproduced (all MEASURED):
- **Rows.** 84,234 rows, 30,864 documents, 61 volumes for 1861-1899; 13,160 rows and 5,314 documents for 1900-1905. Exact.
- **Head grain.** 61,104 head rows from the TEI against the claim's 61,068.
- **POCOM surname rule names one person.** 45,263 against 45,258. The 5-row gap is a regex in the inherited m1a POCOM loader that skips Monroe's one attribute-bearing appointment block.
- **Documents with a suggestion.** 27,387 after #1292 and 24,876 before, of 32,809. Exact. The input really is the post-#1292 after-docs.jsonl (md5 9e18819a…); I did not rebuild the Swift harness.
- **Label reach.** 52,643 rows and 26,512 documents against 52,616 and 26,498. 1900-1905 exact at 8,370 and 4,602.
- **Department part of the corroboration table.** On 15,696 Department-only head rows the claim and I agree row by row on 15,692: 15,178 corroborated and 514 contradicted. That is part of the claimed 37,301 and 2,062. The chief-of-mission part, the location and Secretary-convention narrowings, and the reconciliation against the earlier approximation were NOT re-derived.
- **Legation chapters.** My detector finds 4,497 legation-kind documents (claim 4,473). About half are walked to a parent country title, so the legation rules don't run for them. Rows under a legation title: 5,011, POCOM names one person in 540 (claim 5,015 / 540).
- **1873 proxy.** Re-extracted from the TEI: 843 labelled head rows (52 before), 645 of 647 right by role kind, non-Department 240/242, and the same two errors.
- **1900-1905 header proxy.** Department 1,005 right / 45 wrong; U.S. mission 0 right / 49 wrong (claim 0/33).
- **F. W. Seward class.** 117 head-from rows first-signed F. W.; shown 68 -> 113; the Swift sender regex matches 106; the sender rule decided 0, because all 117 datelines already say Department of State.
- **Hunter class.** 411 rows; shown 269 -> 377; POCOM holds no William Hunter post on any date in the window; Department label on 193 of 197 head-from rows.
- **At-risk fallback.** 2,796 documents on the medium datelined-abroad despatch rule, 593 with a non-Secretary addressee; the sender rule decided 19 documents.

What this means for decisions:
- **Corroboration is not identity evidence.** Both sides of the comparison come from POCOM, so a corroboration count says two rules agree, not that either is right.
- **The label reaches most rows, but its precision is barely evidenced.** The U.S.-mission role is the commonest own role (13,796 from-rows in 1861-1899). Its only positive evidence is 1873: 192/193 over about 25 people in one country-arranged volume pair. Where a 1900-1905 header prints an office on a U.S.-mission-labelled side, the label is never right.
- **The 1873 check tests direction, not place.** Country agreement there is close to circular, because the list heading and the chapter title share the volume's country arrangement.
- **The 91.8% header-proxy figure is mostly a Department figure.** 81% of the judged sides carry a Department label.
- **The label can name an unshown role.** It takes categories from the chosen title's candidates, which include a category Source Explorer doesn't show in 604 documents. Reach is unaffected.
- **Band definition.** "1900-1905" is this program's own cut, not one of the feasibility assessment's bands.

**Verdict: partly confirmed.** Every figure tested holds, but the chief-of-mission corroboration counts were not independently reproduced.

Feasibility is then decided by three things: a precision floor per feature at the grain it shows, a blind-keyed identity sample, and verifiers scored on held-out documents. Two findings stand: markup yields a correspondent index, and identity is not shippable. Claude's defensible role narrows to checking the free layers' candidates, where cost stops binding. Source Explorer's best use after #1292 is a filing-role label that asserts no identity.
keyDeltas: The deciding constraint moves. PersonClusterer's only row source is SELECT … FROM persons (IndexingPipeline.swift:1175; DOCUMENTED, reader), so features kept outside persons, person_mentions, the rollup, the crosswalk and the overrides never reach it. The clusterer gate becomes an isolation invariant test. It returns in full if any entry is ever proposed for the People browser.

Unchanged: the markup layer is a correspondent index (97.8% of the 159,182 documents it reaches carry only from/to header names; MEASURED FA §2.1, TEI-rule 267 vol / 197,534 docs). Also unchanged: identity is not shippable (0 of 300 rows keyed; MEASURED, verified).

Status change: the markup layer's zero wrong names on the M2a gold holds by construction. The gold was seeded with the same 88 editor spans in 64 of 64 documents and the annotator removed none (MEASURED, silver verification). Strict precision equals the kept-exact share, 53/88.

A last-token collapse reduces that to 440,528 pairs in 138,882 docs. 66.8% of added pairs have a row inside a paragraph (verification corrected the 76.1% 'body prose' figure).

firstSlice: 1. Owner reindexes to v51 and re-measures population and orphan figures. This delivers editor identities in the four #1291 volumes.
2. Owner decides: wording and provenance for 'Correspondent from markup' and 'Filing role'; the §5(3) exemption for markup-only carriers; the name-string grain per carrier.
3. Engineer writes the isolation invariant test: no derived writer touches persons, person_mentions, person_rollup_member, the crosswalk or PersonClusterOverride.

4. Build correspondents-from-markup as a Research-rail per-document list and a per-volume section, plus a disclosure on the shipped NLTagger People lens. About 2-3 plus 0.5-1 sessions (INFERRED). Route: a bundled 588,607-byte gzip artifact with xcodegen, or a parse-time table with a reindex.
5. Build deterministic checks: F. W. initials and signature, a listing of acting officers and POCOM gaps, and a census of chapter-title forms. Share the Source Explorer classifier with a generator.

6. Stage and blind-key the samples, identity first. Sha256-lock each blind column; no model pre-fill.
- (a) Identity tier A: 100 two-signal rows, 25 per decade 1861-1899.
- (b) Filing-role label sample.
- (c) Fresh detection sample of about 250 documents from the corpus length distribution.
- (d) The 8 unkeyed M2a documents as held-out.
7. Run local controls on identical inputs: a gazetteer-only arm and a local 27-31B verifier, on the gold and on sample (c).
8. Owner ships or refuses the filing-role label per label kind, against sample (b).

9. Only with authorization and a spend cap: a Claude pilot of the agreement-arm filter and the queue verification. Windows vs whole documents, 3 replicates, pre-registered thresholds, scored on sample (c). About $1.4-1.6 per job on the 64 gold docs with Opus; about $37-40 per Opus run on 250 docs (INFERRED).
10. Owner decides the detected-names tier against a per-band floor, using the sample (c) scores.
11. Only if step 10 passes and a verifier helped: one corpus verification pass, capped at the high scenario (arm filter up to $1,113 Sonnet / $2,865 Opus, batch+cache).
12. Only if identity tier A passes: the POCOM possible-officeholder tier. Tiers B (~380 rows) and C (450-500) for per-class claims.
13. After step 4: a guides prototype over 10-20 chapters, on-device FoundationModels vs Claude, with a citation audit.
ownerDecisions: Name-string grain per carrier: accept or refuse per-document lists; choose per-volume scoping or a 'name string, not person' disclosure for cross-document facets and network nodes.

Wording and provenance for new claim types: correspondent from markup, filing role, detected name, possible identity from filing context, checked by a model, model-written summary. Choose a ninth ProvenanceSource or disclosure sentences. The seal stays tied to authority id.
Grant the §5(3) exemption for markup-only carriers. Pin the pre-1910 population (85 vs 76 volumes) for everything else. Decide whether 1900-1909 is in scope for any identity claim.
Authorize or refuse sending corpus text to a hosted model: scope, models, scripted-batch route, retention. Refusal leaves local models as the only verifier.
Set spend caps per phase: pilot, confirmation, corpus.
Set precision floors per feature and band, with thresholds and the matcher tie-break pre-registered before any model runs.

Keying plan:
- Order: identity tier A and the label sample before any review of machine output.
- Sizes: A 100 / B ~380 / C 450-500; the label sample; a 250-document fresh detection sample.
- Protocol: blind, no model pre-fill; the 8 unkeyed M2a documents kept held-out.
Decide whether any verified entry may ever enter the People browser. If yes, the full clusterer gate and rollup bump return.
Synced user verdicts: keep device-local, or schedule a CloudKit Production deploy.
Bundle or download tier per artifact.
Terms review before any Claude-derived artifact ships.
Approve 'maximum possible use' as a list of separately gated features rather than a single program goal.

corrections.problem: Key and population mixing under one name. 758,194, 1,051,899 and 929,012 use grains.py's surface_key (74 honorifics, stripped repeatedly). 768,928, 1,072,769 and 1,841,697 use census K2 (29 honorifics, stripped once). The word 'queue' names three different sets. The 119,094 boundary-variant finding sits in the Claude-verified-names card as if it inflated the priced job, but the priced queue already drops every span overlapping an agreement span. Its own inflation is VCJ's 122,887 repeated keys.
corrections.correction: Label every pair count with its key. Use three names: 'three-way union pairs (census K2) 1,841,697'; 'census net pool (K2) 1,072,769'; 'priced adjudication queue (grains key; excludes spans overlapping any agreement span) 1,051,899 pairs, 929,012 new at presence grain'. In §3.9 add: 'The 11.1% boundary-variant share applies to the census pool, not to the priced queue.' Report the agreement arm as 768,928 pairs (census K2) or 758,194 (grains key), never both unlabelled.
corrections.evidence: MAG figures (census K2, 29-token list); MCJ 'Job B population ... key = grains.py surface_key (74-token honorific list), not the census K2'; MCJ queue definition 'difference minus spans overlapping any agreement span'; VAG methodProblems (119,094 in the three-way pool); VCJ methodProblems (122,887 repeated keys in the queue).

corrections.location: §4.3 'Other post-#1292 facts' ('POCOM single picks corroborated | 82.4% shown after #1292, against 90.4% for B0 (INFERRED)'); P3 row ('9 in 10 was the Python approximation (90.4%). What Source Explorer shows after #1292 is 82.4%')
corrections.problem: Misleading comparison. B0 is a candidates-without-roll-test arm; S_after is the roll-tested shown arm. The row implies P3's '9 in 10' was an artefact of the approximation, but the merged classifier's own candidates without the roll test also give about 9 in 10.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "Without the roll test the merged classifier corroborates 41,020 of 45,258 single picks (90.6%, T_after), matching P3's approximation (40,907, 90.4%). What Source Explorer shows, with the roll test, rose from 36,269 (80.1%) to 37,301 (82.4%) (MEASURED counts, MSE; shares INFERRED). The gap is the roll test, not the approximation. Either way, 'corroborated' means two rules on the same POCOM register agree."
corrections.evidence: MSE out/merged-rule.json summaries: T_after|1861-1899 corroborated 41,020; A0 36,269; S_after 37,301; B0 40,907; POCOM-one 45,258.

corrections.location: §4.3 P3 row: '#1292 reduced it to 14.1% (INFERRED from RF, SE-DOC-AY). A residual set of glued titles remains (157 known documents).'
corrections.problem: Population mixing. 157 = 148 documents dated 1861–1899 + 9 dated 1900–1905. Both are counted in the SE-DOC-VY scope volumes, yet quoted beside an SE-DOC-AY 1861–1899 share.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "...(14.1%, SE-DOC-AY). Known residual: 148 documents in 1861–1899 scope volumes under glued titles the merged normaliser misses (SE-DOC-VY; a subset, not a census), plus 9 in 1900–1905."
corrections.evidence: MSE figure 'Documents still unread by merged normaliser but read by the Python repair: 148 (1861-1899) + 9 (1900-1905)', population 'live-index export documents in scope volumes'.

corrections.location: §5 step 7 ('Run the local controls ... on the gold and on sample 6(c)') and step 9 ('a Claude pilot ... scored against pre-registered thresholds (N5) on sample 6(c)'; spend 'About $1.4–1.6 per job, Opus 5 on the 64 gold documents; about $37–40 Opus per run on 250 fresh documents')
corrections.problem: (i) The only uncontaminated confirmation set becomes the pilot set. Any prompt, window or threshold iteration on 6(c) contaminates it, contradicting §4.2 ('The 64 documents are a screen, not proof; confirmation needs a fresh sample') and N3. This is the 'pilot before corpus' rule applied to a sample that should stay held out. (ii) The spend cell quotes central estimates only. MCJ's high scenario is $10.2 / $10.1 per job, and P2 put a thinking-heavy pilot at up to about $150, so a cap set from this cell is too low. (iii) $37–40 is RC's R6 estimate for whole-document, detection-shaped requests at corpus-mean length, not the windowed verifier. (iv) The whole-document arm the step requires is unpriced.
corrections.correction: Split step 9 in two. 9a: a screen on the 64 gold documents only; iterate there. Then freeze prompts, windows, thresholds, matcher tie-break and model ids by hash. 9b: one confirmation run of the frozen Claude arms and the frozen local controls on 6(c), with no further tuning. Restate spend as screen high about $10 per job (Opus 5, 3 replicates, standard high; up to about $150 with a generous thinking allowance per P2). Label the confirmation cost as RC's whole-document estimate. Set the cap from high scenarios.
corrections.evidence: S/measure-claude-jobs/summary-costs.md rows E:A-pilot-64docs '0.8 / 1.6 / 10.2' and E:B-pilot-64docs '0.7 / 1.4 / 10.1'; RC R6 ('250 fresh documents at the corpus mean length of 3,439 characters cost Sonnet $14.61-15.83 and Opus $36.53-39.59', whole-document detection rows); P2 ('up to about $150 with a generous thinking allowance').

corrections.location: §5 step 12 ('Only if tier A passes its threshold: the POCOM "possible officeholder" tier (3.11). Tiers B and C for claims about individual classes.'); §3.11 Gates (tier A = 100 rows, 25 per decade)
corrections.problem: Quietly weakens the 'keyed instrument before an identity claim' rule and FA §6.4, which §2.3 says 'tightens'. (i) Tier A samples only the stratum where POCOM surname x year and the chapter post agree, and both read POCOM (VSE). A pass licenses that stratum at most: 37,301 shown rows, not the 45,258 single picks, the 8,642 convention-narrowed rows or the 2,081 location-narrowed rows. (ii) 25 rows per decade cannot meet FA §6.4's '≥ 0.90 pooled and ≥ 0.80 in every 75-row band'. The zero-error Wilson lower bound at n = 25 is 0.8668, and a single error fails. (iii) FA §6.4 also requires a measured per-volume rate at which one surname denotes more than one officeholder, which the step omits.
corrections.correction: Rewrite step 12: "Only if tier A passes: ship the 'possible officeholder' tier for the two-signal-agreement stratum only. Exclude Secretary-convention rows, location-narrowed rows, F. W.-initial rows and all 1861–69 'Seward' rows until tier B passes for those classes. Before shipping, meet FA §6.4: ≥ 0.90 pooled and ≥ 0.80 per band, which needs about 75 rows per band rather than 25 per decade, plus a measured Seward-type rate."
corrections.evidence: FA line 912 (§6.4: '≥ 0.80 in every 75-row band'); MSI/VSI sample_design (0.8668 at n=25; 0.963 at n=100); MSE S_after 1861-1899 (corroborated 37,301; location 2,081; convention 8,642; POCOM-one 45,258); VSE ('Corroborated/contradicted counts compare POCOM with POCOM').

corrections.location: §5 step 11: 'one corpus verification pass, capped at the high scenario' with spend 'Arm filter up to $1,113 on Sonnet 5 or $2,865 on Opus 5, batch+cache'
corrections.problem: (i) Bypasses FA §5(3) 'pilot before corpus, pre-1910 first', which §2.1 gate 3 says tightens: it jumps from a 250-document all-era confirmation to all 267 volumes. (ii) 'High scenario' quotes only the batch+cache low-effort treatment. The standard high-effort high scenario is $4,395 (Sonnet 5) and $11,250 (Opus 5). (iii) No keyed check of the layer the corpus pass actually produces. VCJ: a filter pass yields Claude verdicts, not precision, and a non-deterministic rerun differs from the confirmation replicates.
corrections.correction: Rewrite step 11: "Only if step 10 passes: run the frozen verifier first over the pinned pre-1910 population (85 or 76 volumes). Blind-key a stratified spot sample of its output against the per-band floor, then extend. Cap by treatment: batch+cache low effort up to $1,113 / $2,865 (arm filter, Sonnet 5 / Opus 5); any standard or high-effort run needs its own cap (up to $4,395 / $11,250). Record model id, prompt hash and raw responses (N10)."
corrections.evidence: S/verify-measure-claude-jobs/vcost.json B:agree sonnet-5 high|standard|uncached [371.1, 738.0, 4394.9], opus-5 [780.2, 1789.9, 11250.2]; FA line 820 (§5 row 3); VCJ methodProblems (job B is a filter, not an audit).

corrections.location: §1: 'Cost therefore stops binding'
corrections.problem: Overstated, and contradicts N2 and §7.2 item 12. The headline set's high scenario is $2,265 on Sonnet 5 batch+cache and $22,548 on Opus 5 standard high effort; thinking tokens are unmeasured.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "At central batch estimates, cost is small beside the gates. High scenarios run about 5× central ($444 -> $2,265 on Sonnet 5 batch+cache; up to $22,548 on Opus 5 standard high effort), so every phase still needs a cap (N2)."
corrections.evidence: VCJ vcost.json headline_totals; synthesis N2 and §7.2 item 12.

corrections.location: §3.6 card: 'Identity asserted: None while nodes stay per volume'; Verdict 'Conditional: per-volume nodes once 3.2 exists'
corrections.problem: Contradicts the card's own Quality cell and FA §2.5. W. H. and F. W. Seward were both in office in every year of 1861–69, and G. F. and F. W. Seward in 1876–80. A per-volume 'Seward' node in any of those volumes already merges two officeholders' correspondence into one node.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "Per-volume nodes still fold concurrent namesakes within a volume (the Sewards, 1861–69 and 1876–80). A node must be labelled as a name string as printed, or split by filing role; a measured Seward-type rate is owed before any node is sized by degree." Keep the verdict conditional on that labelling rule (N17), not merely on 3.2.
corrections.evidence: FA line 36 ('two concurrent officeholders in every year of 1861–69 and 1876–80') and lines 459-460 ('W. H. + F. W. ... G. F. + F. W.').

corrections.location: §3.4 Reach: 'This is the one untagged-people surface that already ships.'; Quality: 'The filtered NLTagger store's top corpus strings include 'john' (3,943) and 'chiang kai' (2,454)'
corrections.problem: (i) Contradicted by RA. Already-shipped untagged-people surfaces also include: Office of the Historian volume-level people tags on all 267 untagged volumes (647 assignments: presidents and secretaries of state), shown as chips and filters; full-text search, which the in-app copy points to; and on-device summary templates that name participants. (ii) The lens runs raw NLTagger with no frozen filter, so the filtered store's counts do not describe what it shows.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "One of several untagged-people surfaces that already ship (also: OH volume people tags on all 267 untagged volumes, 647 assignments, MEASURED RA manifest_people_tags.json; full-text search; on-device summary templates, see gaps)." For quality: "Not measured. The lens is unfiltered live NLTagger; the frozen-filter store figures (FA §2.1) are a lower bound on its noise, not a description of it."
corrections.evidence: RA summary item 3 and manifest_people_tags.json (untagged_volumes_with_any_people_tag 267, untagged_people_tags_total 647); RA word-cloud entry (WordCloudTokenizer.swift:157-185, no frozen filter); FA line 272-274 (filtered-control counts).

corrections.location: §3.5 Cost: 'or the label can be computed live in the Research rail with no reindex'
corrections.problem: No support, and it contradicts RA. RA's Research-rail entry says the markup part needs the data layer (reindex). In the live index the untagged volumes carry no from/to marks: person_mentions exist only in the split parts. Only a document-level role derived from header, dateline and section path can be computed live, as Source Explorer does. The label's stated grain, the editor-marked side, cannot.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "A document-level filing role (from header, dateline and chapter path) can be computed live with no reindex. Attaching it to editor-marked from/to sides needs the markup data layer (a bundled artifact or an index table plus a reindex)."
corrections.evidence: RA surface 'Research rail' ('The markup part needs the data layer (reindex)'); RA summary (5,984 person_mentions rows in the 267 = the four #1291 volumes only); RA Source Explorer entry (classification computed live from document_cache.header/dateline + volume_structures).

corrections.location: §3.2 Cost ('The artifact is 2,632,099 bytes, 588,607 with gzip -9 (MEASURED, MAG [V])'); §3.7 Cost ('The artifact is 2,926,099 bytes with gzip -9'); §5 step 4 ('A bundled artifact (588,607 bytes gzipped, MEASURED)')
corrections.problem: Mislabelled as the feature's artifact. These are census.py's grouped one-letter (document, K2) format: lower-cased keys with one honorific stripped, and no display string, from/to direction or stable ids. VAG: 'Format only; no app-shaped size was measured.'
corrections.correction: Say: "A census-format proxy of 588,607 gzip bytes (editor layer) and 2,926,099 (agreement arm) (MEASURED, MAG [V]). The size of an app-shaped correspondents artifact, with display strings, direction and stable ids, is not measured."
corrections.evidence: MAG figure 'T1 agreement arm bundle, grouped one-letter (census ArmAcc format)'; VAG bundle check note ('Format only; no app-shaped ... size was measured').

corrections.location: §3.2 Cost ('about 1 session for a volume-page section, 1–2 for a Research-rail accordion, 0.5–1 for provenance wiring. Staying outside persons drops ...'); §5 step 4 ('Engineer: 2–3 sessions for the list and section')
corrections.problem: Unsupported cost. RA's per-surface estimates presuppose the data layer ('Needs the data layer'). RA sized that layer separately: 2–3 sessions on the parse-time route, 3–4 on the artifact route (generator, bundled artifact, re-apply hook, xcodegen). An isolated carrier still needs a generator or index table and its own re-apply and removal hook, as gate 11 itself says.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "2–3 sessions for the two surfaces (INFERRED, RA), plus an isolated data layer (generator or index table, re-apply and removal hook, stable ids), which is not sized. RA's closest figures are 2–3 sessions (parse-time) and 3–4 (artifact), both including pieces the isolated route drops."
corrections.evidence: RA surfaces 'Shared person data layer' (engineering 2-3 / 3-4 sessions), 'Volume front-matter Persons list' and 'Research rail' (both state dependence on the data layer); synthesis gate 11 ('its own re-apply hook').

corrections.location: §1 ('One assessment figure changes status: the markup layer's zero wrong names on the gold holds by construction'); §4.1 row 'Changes in status'; §4.4 erratum 2
corrections.problem: Overstated as an erratum. FA already identifies the 88 marked spans as the gold's seeds: line 664, 'strict P 0.602 is the title convention (53 exact + 34 title-extended + 1 split of 88 seeds)'; §1.4 item 3, 'seeds included'. The real defect is narrower. FA calls P 1.000 / 0 false keys 'Measured quality' without saying that, once no seed was removed, relaxed precision 1.000 was guaranteed. Also, 'by construction' is only true conditionally: the annotator could have removed seeds and, under anchoring, removed none.
corrections.correction: Reword erratum 2: "FA knew the 88 marked spans were seeds (line 664) but presented presence P 1.000 / 0 false keys as measured quality. Because the annotator, shown those spans, removed none (MEASURED, VSI: 53 kept exactly, 35 boundary-edited, 0 removed), relaxed precision 1.000 follows from that outcome. The figure cannot detect a wrong editor mark and is not an independent precision."
corrections.evidence: FA lines 192 and 664; VSI check 'M2a seeds and the marked arm scored against its own seeds'.

corrections.location: §0 opening: 'No LLM API was called and no corpus text left the machine to produce it.'
corrections.problem: Inaccurate as written, and it pre-empts gate N1. The measuring and verifying agents read corpus text into Claude Code sessions: MSE/VSE quote headers such as 'Earl Russell to Lord Lyons', VAG wrote samples.json, and LP holds 141,512 bytes of identity case reads. Claude Code transmits that text to Anthropic. Gate 2 itself says design-time reading 'is already practised', and RC R9 says those snippets 'travel through the same API'. Treating that practice as needing only 'a stated exception' quietly bypasses the no-API-use-without-authorization rule.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "No scripted LLM or token-count API call was made. Corpus snippets were read inside Claude Code sessions, which send them to Anthropic." Make N1 say explicitly that the owner's authorization must state whether in-session reads of corpus text are covered, and until then it records that they already occurred during this assessment.
corrections.evidence: RC R9 ('The owner-authorization rule should say whether it covers in-session reads, since those snippets travel through the same API'); VSE/MSE examples (at-risk addressee examples); VAG samples.json; LP identity/cases.txt.

corrections.location: §4.1 row 'Dollar lines rescaled from the Ride-Along's per-candidate pricing | §4.c; §7 | Superseded | By the MCJ job prices in §3.'
corrections.problem: Overstated. MCJ priced no identity job over detected surfaces. Its job C covers 13,907 editor-marked from/to rows, and MCJ lists 'an identity-adjudication job over detected (novel) surfaces' as not measured. FA §4.c's R-3 adversarial-tier price covers detector candidates.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "Superseded for editor-marked correspondents only (MCJ job C; RC R4, 22,688 unresolved rows: Sonnet $10 / Opus $24 central). Identity adjudication over detected surfaces remains priced only by FA §4.c's rescale and RC's 301,979-row detector-union shape (Sonnet $137 / Opus $325 central, INFERRED)."
corrections.evidence: MCJ notMeasured ('An identity-adjudication job over detected (novel) surfaces; job C covers editor-marked from/to rows only'); RC R4 cost range.

corrections.location: §3.9 Quality: 'Queue yield on the gold: 58 of 330 queue pairs can add a true new name under lenient overlap, and 241 touch no gold mention'
corrections.problem: A ceiling presented without being called one. 58 counts any-overlap credit, which VCJ says is looser than one-to-one matching, and 241 counts pairs touching no gold mention, not scorer-matched false names. Both are post hoc on 64 documents.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "Post-hoc ceiling on the gold (GOLD, lenient any-overlap credit, looser than the scorer's one-to-one matching): at most 58 of 330 queue pairs could add a true new name (17.6%); 241 overlap no gold mention. A scorer-matched count restricted to the queue was not computed."
corrections.evidence: VCJ check 'Yield ceiling for job A on the gold' (note: 'My lenient figures are looser than one-to-one matching; I did not compute a scorer-matched count restricted to the queue').

corrections.location: §3.9 jobs table, recall row ('Disagreement set perfectly verified: P 0.921, R 0.969'); §4.2 row '(2) Verify the disagreement set for recall, ceiling P 0.921 / R 0.969'
corrections.problem: Incomplete in a way that matters for a per-band floor. RC's figure is editor ∪ agreement arm ∪ a perfectly verified disagreement set. Even with perfect recall verification, 1930–1945 precision stays at 0.772, so the recall job alone cannot meet a per-band floor in the band the floor argument turns on.
corrections.correction: Add: "per band P 0.985 / 0.977 / 0.772 / 0.884; 1930–1945 precision is untouched by the recall job. Only the precision job (P 0.745 -> 1.000 there) moves that band." In §5, order the arm filter before or with any recall job.
corrections.evidence: S/read-claude/disagreement/disagreement.json gold.baseline_plus_perfectly_verified_disagreement per band P 0.985 / 0.9773 / 0.7719 / 0.8841; editor_U_perfectly_filtered_agreement 1930-1945 P 1.0.

corrections.location: §4.2 row 'Test identity only after you key 100 pre-1910 rows, blind': 'The 100 pre-1910 rows hold 12 several-candidate rows, a zero-error lower bound of only 0.7575'
corrections.problem: Ambiguous in a way that misstates the instrument. 0.7575 is the zero-error bound for the 12-row several-candidate subset. For all 100 rows it is 0.963.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "The 100 pre-1910 rows give a zero-error lower bound of 0.963 overall, but hold only 12 several-candidate rows, whose zero-error bound is 0.7575 (MEASURED arithmetic, MSI [V])."
corrections.evidence: MSI sample_design (0.7575 at n=12; 0.963 at n=100); LP identity/gate.json (pre-1910 several 12).

corrections.location: §2.1 gate 10 ('1900–1909 falls into no proposed stratum (MEASURED, VSI)'); §2.4 N15 ('It holds 12,405 untagged heads in 20 volumes')
corrections.problem: (i) 'Falls into no proposed stratum' is a property of a design, so it is INFERRED, not MEASURED. (ii) N15's 20 volumes / 12,405 heads are banded by TEI document year, while §0 says bands follow volume-id year unless a row says otherwise. By volume-id year, TEI-267 holds 15 volumes in 1900–1909.
corrections.correction: Label the stratum statement INFERRED. Write N15 as: "By TEI document year, 12,405 untagged from/to heads in 20 volumes, 68.0% honorific-led (MEASURED, VSI). By volume-id year, TEI-267 holds 15 volumes / 9,912 documents in 1900–1909: 9 / 6,193 in 1900–1905, which Source Explorer covers, and 6 / 3,719 in 1906–1909, which it does not (MEASURED, critique/era_reach.py -> era_reach.json)."
corrections.evidence: VSI head-format check; critique script S/critique/era_reach.py -> S/critique/era_reach.json (total 197,534 reproduces TEI-267; <=1899 32,760 reproduces the band).

corrections.location: §3.13 Reach: '13,907 on the pre-#1292 approximation and 14,495 after #1292 (MEASURED, MCJ; VCJ reproduced both ...)'
corrections.problem: Mislabelled. 14,495 is B_after: the Python title-repair approximation layered over the merged classifier. VCJ says it is 'not "Source Explorer as merged"; only arm A is'.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "13,907 (B0, pre-#1292 approximation); 14,495 (B_after, the same approximation over merged output); 13,252 as Source Explorer shows after #1292 (arm A / S_after); 14,485 for the merged classifier's candidates without the roll test (T_after 2,536 + 2,167 + 9,263 + 509 + 10)."
corrections.evidence: VCJ methodProblems (arm B post-#1292 is not Source Explorer as merged); MSE summaries T_after 1861-1899 and 1900-1905.

corrections.location: §3.5 ('Where identity fails, the role still holds. ... the label reads "the Department of State" for 193 of the 197 head-from rows'); §4.3 P3 row ('The filing role is right for 193 of 197 head-from rows')
corrections.problem: Correctness claimed without support. Nothing keyed checks these labels, POCOM holds no Hunter post in the window, and 194 of the 197 datelines already read 'Department of State', so the label mostly restates the dateline. The count is MEASURED; 'right' and 'holds' are not.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "labelled 'the Department of State' for 193 of 197 head-from rows (MEASURED, MSE [V]), consistent with 194 datelines reading Department of State; correctness is unkeyed."
corrections.evidence: MSE hunter-labels.json; VSE Hunter check ('194 head-from datelines contain Department of State'; POCOM has no post in the window).

corrections.location: §3.2 Quality: '46 of 288 gold keys are a token-suffix of another key in the same document, so an uncollapsed list shows "Seward" beside "William H. Seward" (MEASURED, FA §2.2)'
corrections.problem: Mislabelled population. 46 of 288 are gold keys for all mentions. The markup layer has 79 keys on the gold, so this does not measure duplication in a markup-only list, which is what 3.2 ships.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "Duplication inside a markup-only list is not measured. Among all gold keys, 46 of 288 are a token-suffix of another key in the same document (MEASURED, FA §2.2), and in detected additions 8.9% of added pairs share a last token with an editor key (19.5% in 1861–1899) (MEASURED, MAG [V])."
corrections.evidence: FA §2.2 caveat 1 (gold keys); FA line 663 (markup 0 false keys of 79); MAG T2 last-token figure.

corrections.location: §3.3 Quality: 'Every detected span therefore has an exact body_text offset (5,188 of 5,188 sweep spans and 2,694 of 2,694 NLTagger spans in the first sample; MEASURED [V])'
corrections.problem: Generalises beyond the sample, and omits VOF's decoder caveat.
corrections.correction: Replace with: "Every sampled detected span (two independent 400-document samples) has an exact body_text offset... html.unescape applies HTML5 entity rules; a shipped map should decode by XML rules (VOF)."
corrections.evidence: VOF checks 1–3 and methodProblems ('ENTITY DECODER').

corrections.location: §2.1 gate 20 row: effect 'unchanged', status 'Met'
corrections.problem: Internal contradiction within one row. Also, what the census met is reach and size in a census format, not precision.
corrections.correction: Set effect to 'discharged (reach and census-format size); precision still unmeasured', and note the key (census K2).
corrections.evidence: MAG figures and caveats ('No corpus-scale precision exists'); VAG bundle note.

corrections.location: §5 dependency rule ('Each step needs the one before it unless marked independent') against step 6 ('Can start in parallel with step 4') and §3.11 Gates ('Build and measure the deterministic checks first')
corrections.problem: Step order contradicts itself. Step 6 follows step 5 (the deterministic checks) yet is said to run parallel with step 4. If tier A's stratum is defined after the checks, as §3.11 requires, 6(a) cannot start before step 5.
corrections.correction: Mark 6(b) label sample, 6(c) detection sample and 6(d) held-out M2a as independent. Make 6(a) identity tier A depend on step 5, because strata must exclude F. W.-initial and convention-narrowed rows. Say so in the table.
corrections.evidence: Synthesis §5 table and §3.11 Gates.

corrections.location: §3.11 bullet 'Silver covers post-1910 only' ('Adding crosswalked people who have no POCOM slug gives 0.972 / 0.939 / 0.863 (INFERRED, MSI)') and §7.2 item 15
corrections.problem: Could be read as precision. VSI: it is an agreement rate over heads the OH registry covers, dominated by a few namesake pairs (Lyndon B. / U. Alexis Johnson 649, McGeorge / William P. Bundy 619, Woodrow / Charles S. Wilson 88), and banded by TEI document year. Under the assessment's volume-id key, 1930–1945 is 0.930.
corrections.correction: Add: "agreement over registry-covered heads, not a precision; the errors are concentrated in three namesake pairs; TEI-document-year bands (volume-id key: 1930–1945 0.930) (MEASURED, VSI)."
corrections.evidence: VSI checks 'Negative silver and combined S precision' and 'Silver identity set size by band'.

gaps: The issue's own named surfaces get no disposition. #234 named the People browser, person search, person analytics and the co-mention graph. Surfaces that inherit person rows automatically (Related documents' Shared-people axis, the Collections Persons Index and its exports, the custom-scope person facet) are also unaddressed. None of the 14 candidates is person analytics. The delta should state plainly that isolated carriers deliver none of these surfaces except as new, separate views, and list what folding entries in would re-import: FA §4.a's clusterer gate, the rollup bump, and silent relatedness changes (RA: SharedPersonScorer weight 0.7).

An already-shipped, ungated identity path is missing. On-device FoundationModels summary templates (Diplomatic Exchange: Parties; Meeting Record: KeyParticipants; Individual Role Trace) can name participants in untagged documents from model memory. The output is stored in GeneratedSummary (a CloudKit-synced @Model) and indexed into document_cache.summary_text for full-text search (DOCUMENTED, RA). This is the 'model memory as a source' and 'a confidently wrong person is the worst defect' class, live today, and neither N9 nor any candidate addresses it. It needs a candidate (template wording 'as printed', a disclosure, exclusion from name search) or an explicit owner acceptance.
